changelog:
1080p is back, by asking the way ReVanced asks. Android VR was written off here as needing a login; it does not. It needs the request an application makes rather than the one a web page makes: the app endpoint at youtubei.googleapis.com instead of www.youtube.com, a deviceMake and deviceModel, and none of a browser's Origin and Referer headers - an Oculus user agent carrying a web page's headers is not a client YouTube has ever seen. Asked properly it answered with 22 renditions up to 2160p, every one of them carrying an address.

That matters because the plain Android client no longer carries addresses at all: nineteen adaptive renditions with no url on any of them, and one muxed 360p, which is exactly why trailers had dropped to 360p.

Android VR is also refused a fair part of the time with "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot". That is a gate on the asker, not on the request, and the answer to it is to fall through to the next client rather than to hammer it - so a break gets 360p that day rather than nothing, and the good rendition whenever the gate is open.
description: Lightweight virtual TV channels: deterministic schedules over your own library, tuned in via normal direct playback at the live position. No transcoding, no tuner emulation.
name: LiteTV Channels
